props.title: Terror Out of the Sky

sections.content: **Terror Out of the Sky (1978)** (1978), also known as "The Savage Bees II," rides the wave of nature-horror films that dominated 1970s television following the success of **Jaws** (1975). This made-for-TV sequel to The Savage Bees (1976) exemplifies the era's fascination with killer insect films, alongside theatrical releases like The Swarm (1978) and **The Bees** (1978). These films tapped into growing environmental anxieties and fears about nature's revenge against human interference.

sections.content: The killer bee subgenre emerged from real-world concerns about Africanized honey bees migrating northward through the Americas. **The Deadly Bees** (1966) kicked off the trend, but it was The Savage Bees (1976) that established the TV movie template: isolated community, skeptical authorities, and a race against time to prevent catastrophe. **Terror Out of the Sky** (1978) follows this formula while adding elements of ecological horror that would later influence films like **Piranha** (1978) and **Prophecy** (1979). SUBHEAD: The Nature-Horror TV Movie Boom

Television networks capitalized on environmental fears throughout the 1970s with movies like **Killdozer** (1974), **Locusts** (1974), and **Tarantulas: The Deadly Cargo** (1977). These productions offered scaled-down versions of theatrical disaster films, focusing on intimate threats to small communities rather than global catastrophes. **Terror Out of the Sky** (1978) fits perfectly into this pattern, delivering contained suspense with modest special effects and an emphasis on human drama over spectacle.
